reviews.reason: This remark uses only that separable complete-metric Baire is choice-free over ZF and unrestricted complete-metric Baire is equivalent to DC. The supplier repair changed only the claimed ZF comparison between DMC and DC, so neither premise nor the Banach-space cost conclusion changes.

The only actual use of the Urysohn status remark is the clause that Urysohn's lemma is not provable in ZF or in ZF plus countable choice. The corrected open status of DMC implying DC over ZF does not alter that clause or any separation-chain dependency.

The theorem proves Urysohn's lemma directly from DC and uses the external status remark only to say ZF plus countable choice is insufficient; it explicitly does not claim DC is necessary. Replacing a false ZF DMC-versus-DC strictness assertion by an open-status qualification changes neither the proof nor its choice contract.

This remark says DMC implies Urysohn's lemma and separately that whether Urysohn's lemma implies DMC is open; it never infers a strict relation between DMC and DC over ZF. The supplier's corrected DMC/DC comparison therefore leaves every stated implication, nonimplication, and consistency qualification intact.
